exposure: Intravenous dexmedetomidine administration (before and during cesarean section vs. after delivery vs. not at all)
Three groups: dexmedetomidine before and during delivery (DX), dexmedetomidine after delivery (SC), and no dexmedetomidine (CN)
cohort: 392 women undergoing elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia
finding: Administering intravenous dexmedetomidine before and during elective cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia appears safe and effective, leading to reduced sufentanil and ondansetron consumption, faster lactation onset, and shorter hospital stays.
